slides.title: Definitions Diagnostic –
slides.body:
o Diagnosis: It is the capacity of an electronic system (Control unit), equipped with microprocessor, to carry out a cyclic
check, through the acquisition, processing and comparison of component signals directly or indirectly connected, of
both internal (microprocessor, memory, etc.) and external (sensors and actuators) components belonging to the same
system. The results of the diagnosis, in case of failure (permanent or intermittent) detection through the control unit,
must be recorded in the dedicated error cells of the non-volatile memory.
o Communication protocol: It is the set of rules controlling and allowing the communication between one or more
electronic systems and diagnostic instrument
o Diagnostic instrument: Electronic equipment able to guarantee the communication to one or more electronic
systems provided with diagnosis.
o Error cell: It is a RAM or EEPROM memory cell containing the information (error code, environmental parameters)
relevant to a single trouble
DefinitionsDiagnostic –

slides.title: Performance Diagnostic
General rules Recognition of failures –
Sensor/Actuator failures Recognition of failures –
Other failures Recognition of failures –
slides.body:
o Electronic system failures: the electronic control system must also have self-diagnosis strategies
for the electronic system components within the control unit that take part in permitting regular
operations.
o Power supply failures: the electronic system must be able to diagnose any missing power supply
connections, save the related error code in its memory and turn on the warning lamp if foreseen and
available. If correct operation is guaranteed by a certain voltage range, the system that is supplied
out of range must inhibit those diagnoses as they could generate false emergency recognition.
o Mechanical part failures: compatibly with hardware and software feasibility, it must be possible to
keep under control, measure and control variations in mechanical parameters through the system
sensor assembly or lines dedicated to monitoring.
Other failuresRecognition of failures –

C.A.N. failures Recognition of failures –
slides.body:
The Nodes connected to the CAN network that diagnose and store diagnostic information must
provide the following 2 bit coded information via the CAN network:
o GenericFailSts (Stored DTC);
o CurrentFailSts (Active DTC);
Usually, these information are present in the message that each ECU sends on CAN BUS with
the description of the identifier as STATUS_C_XXX

slides.title: Node FAULTY Possible CAN failures –
slides.body:
The implementation of this diagnosis is:
o MANDATORY: when one of the messages received has a shorter length;
o OPTIONAL if a received message is missing (in case of reception of more
than one message) or receives a message in an incorrect format (e.g.
wrong CRC or MC).
There must be only one DTC assigned to each source node;
The detection of this error must be disabled during the mute period that
follows a bus-off condition.
The diagnosis of this error must be disabled as soon as the receiving Node
detects a Node Mute error (on itself), and must be re-enabled when the Node
Mute error becomes “not present”.
Node FAULTYPossible CAN failures –

slides.title: Node MUTE Possible CAN failures –
slides.body:
Node A recognizes that it is disconnected from the network. Node A can control its
CAN Controller error status (error passive, warning), and the type of CAN Controller
error (ACK error). In case of node MUTE, only the DTC related to the single node
must be stored and the diagnosis of node absent and node faulty must be inhibited as
long as the node mute condition persists because the diagnosis on other nodes
carried out from a node with errors on its own controller should not be considered
significant.
o the detection of this fault must disable the detection of the Node ABSENT and
Node FAULTY;
o the detection time for this diagnosis must always be greater than the maximum
value of the silence period for the bus-off specified for the source node;
o the detection time for this fault must be shorter than those adopted for Node
ABSENT and Node FAULTY faults.
Node MUTEPossible CAN failures –

slides.title: BUS-Off Possible CAN failures –
slides.body:
Node A detects a bus-off condition. Node A controls its CAN
Controller error status (bus-off). In case of bus OFF, only the
DTC related to the single node must be stored.
- During the mute period that must follow the detection of a
bus-off, all faults connected to CAN communication must be
disabled
- The Bus OFF event counter must be increased by one unit
each time that the CAN controller enters the Bus OFF status
in the same cycle.
BUS off Performance maturation timing is stated in: minimum
time is 800ms and maximum time is 1500ms for each type of
CAN BUS
BUS-OffPossible CAN failures –

slides.title: Structure Error memory –
StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMask Error memory –
slides.body:
This byte takes on a specific meaning depending on if it is integrated in the tester request (Status Mask or in the ECU response (Status
Of DTC). If inserted in the diagnostic instrument request to the ECU, it indicates on which Bits the comparison should be carried out
with regard to the status values of each DTC, whereas in the central unit response, it unequivocally identifies the error status of each
DTC. The definition of each status Mask or Status Of DTC Bit coincides as they have the same meaning independently of their context;
the description follows:
- bit 0: testFailed
- bit 1: testFailedThisMonitoringCycle
- bit 2: pendingDTC
- bit 3: confirmedDTC
- bit 4: testNotCompletedSinceLastClear
- bit 5: testFailedSinceLastClear
- bit 6: testNotCompletedThisMonitoringCycle
- bit 7: warningIndicatorRequested
StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMaskError memory –

slides.title: StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMask Error memory –
slides.body:
bit 0: testFailed
In the absence of a fault in a present status or after a ClearDiagnosticInformation the Bit status, before executing a test, must be = 0
The bit must always indicate the result of the last test completed during the Monitoring Cycle:
- 1 = the result of the last completed test is Failed (fault present)
- 0 = the result of the last completed test is Passed (fault not present)
bit 1: testFailedThisMonitoringCycle
The default status, before the recognition of an anomaly or after a ClearDiagnosticInformation request, must be = 0.
The bit must indicate the result of the last test completed during the current Monitoring Cycle:
- 1 = during the current Monitoring Cycle at least one (1) test was completed whose result was Failed (fault detected).
- 0 = during the current Monitoring Cycle one (1) test has not yet been completed or all the completed tests have had a Passed result (no
fault detected).
StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMaskError memory –

slides.title: StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMask Error memory –
slides.body:
bit 2: pendingDTC
The default status, before the recognition of an emergency or after a ClearDiagnosticInformation request, must be = 0.
The bit status must be set to 1 as soon as a test with a Failed result has been completed (emergency recognition).
The bit indicates the presence of an anomaly in the current Monitoring Cycle or during the previous Monitoring Cycle or the absence of an anomaly in the current and previous cycles:
- 0 = at the end of the current and previous Monitoring Cycles all completed tests have had a Passed result (a fault was never detected).
- 1 = during the current or previous Monitoring Cycle at least one (1) test was completed whose result was Failed (fault detected).
bit 3: confirmedDTC
The default status, before the recognition of an emergency, must be = 0.
The bit status must be set to 1 as soon as a test with a Failed result has been completed (emergency recognition).
The bit must indicate if the fault is present in the error memory (in the not volatile memory or in RAM while waiting to be stored in the not volatile memory):
- 1 = the DTC was confirmed at least once after the last clearDiagnosticInformation request and the criteria of automatic deletion from the not volatile memory were not satisfied.
- 0 = the DTC was NOT confirmed even once after the last clearDiagnosticInformation request or the criteria of automatic deletion from the not volatile memory were satisfied (the DTC was
deleted from the not volatile memory).
StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMaskError memory –

slides.title: StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMask Error memory –
slides.body:
bit 6: testNotCompletedThisMonitoringCycle (optional)
The default status, at the start of each Monitoring Cycle, must be = 1.
The bit must indicate if the test was ever executed and completed during the current Monitoring Cycle (or executed and completed after the last
clearDiagnosticInformation request):
- 1 = during the current Monitoring Cycle, the test of the diagnosis line under examination was never completed.
- 0 = during the current Monitoring Cycle the test was completed at least once independently of its result or the test was not yet activated due to unsatisfied enabling
conditions.
bit 7: warningIndicatorRequested
The default status must be = 0.
The bit status must be set to 1 when the validated DTC activates the warning lamp.
The bit must indicate if the validated DTC is activating the switching on of the related lamp/message:
- 1 = the warning lamp is active; the DTC foresees the switching on of the warning lamp.
- 0 = the warning lamp is NOT active, the DTC does NOT foresee the switching on of the warning lamp or the enabling conditions were not satisfied (example error status
or number of cycles for activation NOT reached).
StatusOfDTC/DTCStatusMaskError memory –

slides.title: Snapshot record Error memory –
slides.body:
The DTCSnapshotRecord is composed of the environmental parameter identifiers with the
corresponding values frozen upon validation of the fault at the first and last occurrence.
The first 4 parameters of each DTCSnapshotRecord are obligatory for each system and DTC.
At the first validation of a fault, the first associated DTCSnapshotRecord must contain the data recorded
at the moment of its first validation that remain until the DTC is deleted from the error memory.
The subsequent validations of the same fault (understood as devalidation and revalidation of the same
fault - transition of Bit 0), will enable the composition of the second and last associated
DTCSnapshotRecord that must contain the data recorded at its last validation
Snapshot recordError memory –

slides.title: Extended data record Error memory –
slides.body:
The DTCExtendedDataRecord contains the following fields (see definition in the document):
o EventCounter (obligatory for all systems):
o Cycle to switch warning lamp OFF (obligatory for systems that manage a warning lamp)
Any other specific fields must be agreed upon between the Supplier and the EE - EAI systems engineer
for each individual application and specified in the relative CDD document produced with CANdela.
Extended data recordError memory –

slides.title: Event counter (no powertrain nodes) Error memory –
slides.body:
The eventCounter parameter must be set to 40 decimals in the following cases:
o at the moment in which the error cell is stored for the first time (coinciding with the simultaneous transition from
0 to 1 of confirmedDTC (bit 3 of status Of DTC) and of testFailed (bit 0 of StatusOfDTC).
o each time there is a transition from 0 to 1 of testFailedThisMonitoringCycle (Bit 1 of statusOfDTC) having
confirmedDTC (bit 3 of status Of DTC) already at a value of 1 (error already stored previously in the error
memory).
o The counter must be decreased by one unit at each Key ON if during the previous monitoring cycle (including
the shut-down phase) the related error assumed the “NOT Present” status for the entire cycle (testFailed - bit 0
of StatusOfDTC set to 0).
o The error cell must be deleted from the error memory when the eventCounter reaches the value of 0.
Event counter (no powertrain nodes)Error memory –

slides.title: Event counter (Powertrain & EOBD) Error memory –
slides.body:
The PowerTrain area electronic systems that have an impact on vehicle emissions must manage the “eventCounter”
information according to the current European directive. In particular, the eventCounter must follow the following rules:
o the event counter must be set to 40 decimals at the moment in which the error cell is stored for the first time (coinciding
with the simultaneous transition from 0 to 1 of confirmedDTC (bit 3 of status Of DTC) and of testFailed (bit 0 of
StatusOfDTC) and each time that there is a transition from 0 to 1 of testFailedThisMonitoringCycle (Bit 1 of
statusOfDTC) having confirmedDTC (bit 3 of status Of DTC) already at a value of 1 (error already stored previously in
the error memory).
o The counter will be decreased, within the monitoring cycle, if the MIL status is OFF at the beginning of the driving cycle,
the test was completed with the result Passed and a warm UP is completed
o The error cell must be deleted from the error memory when the eventCounter reaches the value of 0 (cell not visible to
the diagnostic instrument).
Event counter (Powertrain & EOBD)Error memory –

slides.title: Cycle to switch lamp off Error memory –
slides.body:
The Electronic Systems that manage at least one warning lamp and/or message must manage the Cycle to
switch warning lamp OFF parameter.
This parameter indicates the number of cycles (Monitoring cycle) that remain until the deactivation of the warning
lamp, the following rules are valid (see example in fig. 3 and 4):
- if the fault does not foresee the lamp turning on, the parameter must always assume the value of 0;
- if the fault does foresee the lamp turning on, the parameter:
- must be set to the number of cycles foreseen for turning off the warning lamp at the moment in which it is activated
(for powertrain systems it is 3 for applications with EOBD diagnosis and 1 for systems without EOBD diagnosis)
- must be decreased by one (1) unit at each consecutive error free monitoring cycle;
- must be set to 0 in the moment in which the warning lamp is deactivated (warning lamp OFF);
- must indicate the number of cycles necessary for turning off the warning light if the system is not in one of the above
described conditions.
Cycle to switch lamp offError memory –

slides.title: Fault validation/de-validation filtering Error memory –
slides.body:
o Each diagnosis line (DTC) must be specified in terms of timing/counter and enabling conditions for the
necessary filtering in order to avoid not significant detections due to typical vehicle disturbances.
o It is a good practice to provide a series of time and counter variables for each diagnostic line in order to easily
calibrate both validation as well as devalidation without having to make changes to the control unit sw.
o Based on the type of ECU hardware, the Supplier must make the detailed information about the anomaly
available, properly distinguishing the symptom of each DTC from among the electric type diagnoses and the
plausibility diagnoses, in addition, each DTC must identify a specific component (sensor / actuator) with
exception of the plausibility diagnoses where the original cause of the anomaly cannot be identified with
certainty, in this case the Supplier will agree with the system engineer upon the selection of the DTC and the
specific symptom.
Fault validation/de-validation filteringError memory –

slides.title: Erasing Error memory –
slides.body:
o It must be possible to delete, through a specific diagnostic command, the entire contents of the error
memory (both volatile and non-volatile memory);
o The cancellation of the volatile memory must occur upon reception of the diagnostic instrument
command, all of the memory cells related to faults having Bit 0 TestFailed of status Of DTC must be
reset to 0 “Fault Not Present”;
o The error cells in which the eventCounter decreases down to 0 must be deleted autonomously by the
electronic system. Other types of automatic cancellation are not permitted in addition to those cited
ErasingError memory –

slides.title: Recovery strategies Error memory –
slides.body:
At the verification of each anomaly, the electronic system must be able to implement the required recovery
strategy. These strategies have the purpose of:
o avoiding further damage to the system;
o permitting system operation, even if with degraded performances;
o protecting the safety of the driver and the system in general.
In case of sensor malfunctions, the electronic system will replace the values obtained from the faulty
sensors using the recovery values agreed upon with the systems engineer or, if possible, will calculate
them obtaining them indirectly by reading/processing other parameters.
In case of actuator emergencies, the recovery strategies to adopt depend on the actuator in question.
All the recovery strategies, both those related to sensors as well as those related to actuators, are
differentiated by component type and must therefore be agreed upon with the systems engineer on a case
by case basis and specified in detail in the Cdd CANdela and diagnostic function summary.
Recovery strategiesError memory –

slides.title: Warning lamp management (PWT & EOBD) Error memory –
slides.body:
The MIL warning lamp must remain on from Key ON until the engine is started and must be turned off after the
engine is ignited if no faults are detected. The operation of the MIL warning lamp is described in the current
European directive.
The turning on of the MIL lamp may be of the type On-1, On-3 or Off depending if the outfitting was
type-approved according to EOBD regulations or with the exclusion of the EOBD diagnostic strategies. The MIL
activation modality is described briefly below:
- ON-1 : the MIL is activated immediately upon error validation;
- ON-3 : the MIL is activated at the third cycle if the error was validated for three consecutive monitoring cycles;
- OFF : the activation of the MIL is not foreseen in any case for this type of error as it is not considered serious for
safety purposes and is not emission relevant.
Warning lamp management (PWT & EOBD)Error memory –

slides.title: Engineering parameter transmission RDI –
slides.body:
Engineering parameter transmissionRDI –
All engineering parameters generated by the sensors and processed by the electronic system as well as some
parameters calculated and used for control and implementation must be available on the diagnostic link.
These parameters will be made available on the diagnostic link, upon proper request, individually or in a group
(with a specific command); in addition, they must be accessible in the key ON status, with the motor running and
at any vehicle speed.
In case of errors on a certain component, the related parameter that is transmitted must be the one actually read
by the sensor and not the recovery parameter used by the electronic system.
If one or more parameters are not present in an application (version, outfitting), upon request by the instrument
of that specific parameter, the control unit must respond with a negative response whose significance must be
“parameter not available” (Nack 0x31).

slides.title: Active diagnosis I/O Control –
slides.body:
The active diagnosis is a function that, through specific diagnostic controls, permits to control the system actuators or modify the value of
magnitudes of system output that is transmitted to other electronic systems.
During active diagnosis, the electronic system must implement the diagnostic strategies present during normal system operations.
Active diagnosis must be foreseen in the following situations:
- the component is not continuously monitored by the ECU or must be diagnosed only in particular conditions that are difficult to reach; through
active diagnosis it is instead possible to control the component to immediately verify its functionality by reading the error memory and through
specific engineering parameters
- component activation must be verified by sound or sight
- the component must be calibrated
whereas it must be avoided:
- on signals present on CAN networks that are used for plausibility controls from other electronic systems; in fact plausibility diagnostic controls
should not enter into action when the surrounding situation is not correct.
Active diagnosisI/O Control –

slides.title: function Statistical –
slides.body:
functionStatistical –
The diagnostic functions requested of the system may include statistical functions that permit to
reconstruct the history of the vehicle, the electronic system or information that can be used to
reconstruct the use of the system itself. Information can also be stored regarding the total number of
missions, the number of missions in which anomalies have been verified, the number of actuations
of a particular component and anything considered necessary by departments that use the
functions. The main statistical function are:
- Engine Overspeed” Function
- “Odometer” Function

slides.title: Calibration, settings, learning Routine –
slides.body:
Calibration, settings, learningRoutine –
Normally, each control unit / component must guarantee correct functionality as soon as it is installed on the vehicle and powered. However,
there are particular cases for which, in order to guarantee perfect functionality, procedures must be carried out using the diagnostic
instruments. For example, the following list is provided:
- programming keys and/or remote controls;
- parameter characteristic learning (throttle body, phonic wheel, gear position, mixture title… );
- sensor and/or actuator calibration (steering angle, radar beams…);
- operations resulting from or necessary for disconnecting/connecting control units/components (odometer, service intervals, transmission oil
depressurization…
If not done properly, all of these procedures can jeopardize correct system operation and as a result must be defined in the document produced
with CANdela in great detail. Therefore, the Supplier must indicate for each procedure:
- why it must be executed.
- when it must be executed.
- which operation must be performed by repair shop personnel (if foreseen).
- which conditions / sequences must be respected to execute the procedure.
- which commands the diagnostic instrument must send.
- which results does the control unit send to the instrument for each command received.
- which time periods must be respected.
- The conditions in which the procedure appears to be correctly completed.

slides.title: Car Configuration PROXI
slides.body:
Car ConfigurationPROXI
End Of Line programming is used to limit the number of different systems to be produced for satisfying the product grid
requirements, when the differences among various configurations of a certain system can be managed by changing one or more
parameters in the SW.
The parameters are changed through the trasmission of the customizing data.
The data package forming the system configuration data is called PROXI file.
PROXI – Programming and configuration of integrated systems
The EOL programming can be executed only using diagnosis protocol and funtions, so it will be possible to program only
systems equipped with standard diagnosis on can network.

slides.title: Car Configuration PROXI
slides.body:
Car ConfigurationPROXI
The master node of th proxi is the body computer (BCM).
A secondary master node, usually the instrument cluster (IPC), is used for backup functions.
The master node stores all vehicle configuration information and allows the diagnostic tool to read them.
The other nodes taking part to the proxi procedure store only the information directly concerning them, and only when the writing
phase is properly completed, they store such informations in their permanent memory, activating their own functionalities
according with it.

slides.title: EOL Programming file format PROXI
slides.body:
EOL Programming file formatPROXI
The set of all the informations transmitted to the nodes taking part in the PROXI procedure is called PROXI file.
The PROXI format can be .BYT, .EOL, .EPLUS, .HEX.
For each integrated system and for its application to each model, targeted specification document called PROXI programming
targeted specification is issued, which will describe the format of coding the proxi file.
It compries a binary file in which each single bit has a meaning consistent with the format defined by the specification.

slides.title: CRC Check PROXI
slides.body:
CRC CheckPROXI
In order to avoid mismatches between the nodes in the car, is required implementation of a CRC check.
During the generation or modification of the PROXI file, the tool must check from byte 26 to the end of the PROXI file based on
a polynomial calculation of CRC-16.
The result must be written inside the configuration code.
The nodes that receive the procxi must:
- Calculate the CRC from byte 26 to the end of proxi file
- Compare the result with the values in the configuration code
- Accept the proxi file in case of positive result of the comparison or refuse it in case of negative results of the comparison

slides.title: Check configuration PROXI
slides.body:
Check configurationPROXI
The master node is requested to analyze the integrty and coherence of the configuration of each control unit involved, and to
collect data regarding the system status.
The procedure to carry out this task is called check configuration, and involves all the nodes that take part in proxi procedure.
The master node sends the CFG_DATA_CODE_REQUEST message to the network, transmitting its own configuration code.
After receiving the CFG data request, all the nodes that take part to the proxi will send CFG_DATA_CODE_RSP_XXX
message.
The master will analyze the content, and if it is equal to the one stored, then the check configuration will be OK.
Configuration check is performed at every transition to key ON.

slides.title: Check configuration PROXI
slides.body:
Check configurationPROXI
The check configuration can fails if:
- One or more nodes have not responded with its own coded CFG_DATA_CODE_RSP_XXX
- Unexpected responses are received from one or more nodes (nodes not involed in proxi)
- Value of EOL signal not the expected one
- Configuration codes received are different to its own stored code
If the check fails , then the master node may repeat the cycle 3 times before to raise a fail.

slides.title: Check configuration fail snapshot AA PROXI System Diagnosis snapshot A1 PROXI
slides.body:
Check configuration fail snapshot AAPROXI
It is the copy of $40 A2 END OF LINE STATUS , carried out in case of a negative configuration check.
The RDI is $40 AA.
The information contained must be preset to 0 and be reset whenever the configuration check fails and reset when a new
configuration check ends positive.
System Diagnosis snapshot A1PROXI
The system diagnosis function is used to synthesizing inside the Can master node a certain number of diagnostic information,
used with database purpose.
The main data are related to the presence of fault in the ECU, present or stored in memory.

slides.title: EOL status snapshot A2 PROXI
slides.body:
EOL status snapshot A2PROXI
The snapshot contains information on system status after each CONFIGURATION CHECK.
The service to read it is the RDI $40 A2
In detail, the snapshot contains the following information:
- Config_CAN_System: nodes configured in the proxi file, as present on CAN Bus
- Config_EOL_CAN_System: nodes configured in the PROXI file as participant
- Active can systems: nodes active on network
- EOL_CAN_system: nodes that take part in proxi procedure, update their network management message with EOL=1
- EOL_OK_CAN: nodes with EOL=1, that correctly responds to check configuration.
Not all the nodes configured as present, must take part to the proxi procedure.

slides.title: Feedback for PROXI writing KO PROXI
slides.body:
Feedback for PROXI writing KOPROXI
The Nodes receiving the PROXI file must check its content. This procedure, through controls coherent with the diagnostic
protocol foreseen, can end with a positive or negative outcome.
Basically the reason of the reject are: file not conforming with the requirements, file not coherent with the nature of the node
receiving or CRC caluculation not OK.
The type of check for PROXI file are:
- Configuration Code format check� check configuration procedure KO
- Null format check � ASCII stings are alligned to the left and if empty spaces have to be filled, the characters are null (0x20)
- Date format check � the format is YYYY/MM/DD
- Hardware compatibility check � nodes relevat to information included in this field must carry out a coherence checke with
their own hw (i.e. proxi temperature sensor present, but hw of the Ecu not populated)
- Invalid value check � files containing information defined as invalid shall be rejected
- Proxi compatibilty check � coherence information shall respect coherence tables, i.e. proxi table requires dependences of
two or more parameters.

slides.title: UDS Service PROXI
slides.body:
UDS ServicePROXI
The proxi is a stored parameter, both for the master and all nodes taking part in proxi procedure.
To read it the service used is $22.
The parameters to read are:
20 24 � CAR proxi data, stored by the master node
20 23 � ECU proxi data, contains the proxi data read by the single ECU.
To write it the service is $2E

slides.title: Electronic systems re-programming ECU sw Download –
slides.body:
Electronic systems re-programmingECU sw Download –
Re-programming is the operation allowing diagnostic instrument to send informations to the system, which receives,
controls and stores them.
An ECU can be re-programmed, by flashing on it a new sw.
The main operations performed by the diagnostic tool during the download are:
- Erase the EEPROM
- Transfer data to the ECU

slides.title: Sections and blocks SW structure
slides.body:
Sections and blocksSW structure
A sw is generally structured in blocks.
The main type of block are:
- Bootloader
- Application
- Calibration

slides.title: Kit Files Download
slides.body:
Kit FilesDownload
- .BIN file – data file
Containing code and data to be downloaded.
It contains all flash EEPROM data.
- .PRM file – parameter file
Containing all the parameters used by protocol during reprogramming (i.e. target address, access
mode, security access parameters…) and the fingerprint to update
- .IDX file – index file
Containing all operations necessary to match a pair of data + patameter files.
It also contains the informations necessary to check if the download is executable or not,
depending on the identifications of the ECU to flash.

slides.title: Preliminary operations Download
slides.body:
Preliminary operationsDownload
Before to download the sw, the tool performs some preliminary operations to check if the flashing is
available.
During operation check, the whole identification block of the ECU must be available.
For example if the HW is not compatible with the one in the .idx file, then the download won’t start,
to avoid problems on the ECU.

slides.title: Data transfer flow – Tester to all functional addressing Download
slides.body:
Data transfer flow – Tester to all functional addressingDownload
Before to start a download procedure, the tester sends in functional addressing, some requests to all the
ECU present on the same can network.
During a download a minimum level of busload must be guaranteed.
Extended Diagnostic Session
Control DTC setting ($85)
Communication Control ($28)

slides.title: Data transfer flow – Tester to ECU Download
slides.body:
Data transfer flow – Tester to ECUDownload
Programming Session ($1002)
Security access seed&key ($27)
Write sw fingerprint ($2E)
Routine Flash Erase ($FF00)
Request Download ($34)
Transfer Data ($35)
Transfer exit ($36)
check dependencies ($FF01)
ECU Hard Reset ($1101)

slides.title: Data transfer flow – End of flashing sequence Download
slides.body:
Data transfer flow – End of flashing sequenceDownload
Once the flashing procedure has been performed, new identifications will be available on ECU
electronic label, with updated fingerprint (depending on the type of we downloaded: boot,
application, calibration)
After the download ended, the system must update the following data, at the following Key On:
- Number of flash re-programming
- Odometer content to the last F-ROM update
